title: disjoint-set union and connectivity maintenance
concepts: Disjoint-set union (DSU), also called union-find, maintains a partition of elements into non-overlapping equivalence classes and answers whether two elements share a component.
Find returns a representative for an element's set; union merges two sets only when their representatives differ.
Path compression rewrites nodes along a find path to point nearer the representative, while union by size or rank limits tree height during merges.
Together, path compression and union by size/rank give amortized O(α(n)) operation time, where inverse Ackermann α grows so slowly that it is effectively constant for practical input sizes.
DSU supports incremental edge additions and connectivity checks but does not naturally support deleting edges or enumerating a shortest path.
A failed union when adding an undirected edge indicates its endpoints were already connected, which can detect cycle creation in incremental connectivity settings.
Component metadata such as size can be stored at representatives and updated on union; representative identity itself has no semantic meaning.
Kruskal's minimum spanning tree algorithm uses DSU to reject edges that would connect vertices already in the same component.

practiceProblems.name: Redundant Connection
patterns: cycle edge joins an existing component
practiceProblems.statement: A graph began as a tree on n vertices labeled 1 through n, then one new edge between distinct vertices was added. Given the resulting n-edge connected graph with no repeated edges, return the edge that occurs last in the input among those whose removal restores a tree.
constraints: Each edge has two labels with 1 <= a < b <= n
No repeated edges; the graph is connected

practiceProblems.name: Accounts Merge
practiceProblems.statement: Each account begins with a name followed by one or more email addresses. Accounts sharing any email belong to the same person, transitively. Return merged accounts with each person's emails sorted; account output order is arbitrary. Equal names alone do not imply identity.
constraints: Names contain English letters and emails are valid

practiceProblems.name: Number of Provinces
practiceProblems.statement: Given a symmetric n by n 0/1 matrix where a 1 indicates a direct connection between cities, return the number of provinces, meaning connected components under direct-or-indirect connectivity.
constraints: Matrix is n by n; entries are 0 or 1

practiceProblems.name: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
patterns: connect stones sharing a row or column
practiceProblems.statement: Stones occupy unique integer coordinate points. A stone may be removed while another remaining stone shares its row or column. Return the maximum number removable.
constraints: No two stones share a coordinate point

practiceProblems.name: Satisfiability of Equality Equations
practiceProblems.statement: Each equation is x==y or x!=y for lowercase single-letter variables. Return whether some integer assignment satisfies all equations.

practiceProblems.name: Min Cost to Connect All Points
practiceProblems.statement: Given distinct planar integer points, connect every pair by a network whose unique simple path connects each pair, minimizing the sum of Manhattan-distance edge costs. Return the minimum cost.
